sources: Gadi Eisenkot, Yashar party leader and former IDF chief of staff, television interview (i24NEWS, via Iran International/Axar and Eastora)
fault_line: Degrade or topple: is Eisenkot's 'destroy the programmes, not the regime' line a credible war aim, or a dodge that leaves Tehran standing?

sections.what_happened: Eisenkot said toppling the Islamic Republic would be a service to humanity, but 'making it an objective of war would be wrong' / 'is not the right thing to do'. The proper military objectives, he said, were destroying Iran's nuclear and missile programmes and its regional proxy forces: 'And I know how to do that.' On Gaza he pledged that if elected he would either destroy Hamas or dismantle its military and governing capabilities within 18 months. He called Netanyahu 'delusional' over the portrayal of Iran's nuclear capabilities and said Netanyahu knew Iran had not possessed nuclear weapons; available pre-war assessments did not establish Tehran had assembled a nuclear weapon, though the IAEA documented a large highly-enriched-uranium stockpile and unresolved safeguards concerns (Eastora context). He also pushed back on Trump's Netanyahu endorsement: 'only the citizens of Israel' determine Israel's prime minister. This is a campaign position on election eve, not a government policy decision -- Eisenkot is a challenger, not the incumbent.
sections.what_verified: Iran International (T3, exile/opposition provenance) carries the interview via Axar; i24NEWS itself and Eastora have NO declared tier in the registry and are reported with attribution only, not counted. No second declared family retrieved in-window.
sections.what_disputed: Netanyahu's counter-position, already on record today, is that Eisenkot's line amounts to accepting a nuclear-armed Iran -- Eisenkot rejects that reading. The 18-month Hamas pledge is a campaign promise with no plan, force structure or coalition behind it yet; neither bloc is projected to reach 61 seats (recorded 1800-01).
sections.why_matters: 'I KNOW HOW TO DO THAT' -- the challenger draws his Iran red line on election eve: destroy the nukes, the missiles and the proxies -- but do NOT make regime change the war's objective.
